name: West Virginia
$scopeNote: WIRED TO CALC-CODE (2026-08-21, follow-up pass): originally a DATA-ONLY pass (Scott: 'do the Dakotas and the Virginias, just for the data'), left unwired deliberately. Built out once Scott asked to close PA reciprocity's open items. West Virginia's real structure: a 5-bracket progressive percentage-method table (2.11%-4.58%) with a genuinely unusual TWO-TABLE selection mechanic (not marital-status-driven), a 5-state reciprocity cluster (the largest in this project), and flat per-week municipal 'City Service Fees' in several cities -- a structurally different local-tax shape from every other local tax modelled so far (a flat dollar amount, not a percentage of wages). IMPORTANT DIFFERENCE FROM VIRGINIA: WV's own IT-100.2A publishes genuine, independently-set PER-PERIOD tables (weekly/biweekly/semimonthly/monthly/daily/annual, all 6, times both earner tables = 12 full tables) rather than one annual formula meant to be divided -- re-fetched and fully transcribed all 12 this pass (closing a previously-disclosed gap outright, not approximating around it) rather than deriving per-period figures from the annual table the way this engine does for VA/DC/NJ/DE, since a spot check showed WV's own period boundaries do NOT cleanly divide from the annual ones (e.g. annual $7,500 / 52 = $144.23, but the source's own weekly table boundary is $144 flat -- a small but real independently-set figure, not a rounding of the annual one).

Wage base ($9,500, unchanged for several years) and new-employer rate (2.7%) rest on consistent secondary-source agreement, not a direct government figure this pass -- a genuine access limitation, not an under-effort, same class of gap as this project's New Hampshire file.

withholdingStructure.mechanism: Subtract a flat per-period dollar amount PER EXEMPTION CLAIMED (WV/IT-104's own count: 1 for self if claimed, up to 2 for married if not claimed elsewhere, plus 1 per dependent) from gross wages, then look up the result in one of TWO 5-bracket progressive tables -- selection is NOT based on marital status directly, but on an employee ELECTION (IT-104 Line 5): the 'Two Earner/Two or More Jobs' table applies by DEFAULT (i.e. whenever Line 5 is unchecked, regardless of actual marital status), and has LOWER bracket thresholds (withholds MORE); checking Line 5 (available only to Single/HoH/married-with-nonemployed-spouse employees on ONE job) switches to the 'Optional One Earner/One Job' table, which has thresholds exactly 4/3 (=1.3333...) times the two-earner table's at every tier and withholds LESS. This selection mechanic -- an employee opt-IN to a lower-withholding table, defaulting to the higher one -- is structurally different from every other state built in this project (all of which select a table by declared filing status, not by an earner-count election).
withholdingStructure.exemptionAmountNote: Identical across BOTH the two-earner and one-earner tables -- only the bracket thresholds/bases differ, not the per-exemption subtraction.

brackets.$comment: All 12 tables (6 periods x 2 earner types) transcribed directly from IT-100.2A (March 2026 revision, re-fetched 2026-08-21) -- these are the source's OWN independently-published per-period tables, not derived from the annual one. Dispatch (westVirginiaWithholding() in src/taxes/state.ts) looks up the table matching input.payFrequency directly; no annualize-then-divide step exists for WV.
brackets.note: Both tables' per-period boundaries are INDEPENDENTLY published, not derived from the annual figure -- verified this pass by direct comparison: annual $7,500/52 = $144.23, but the source's own weekly boundary is $144 flat (a real, if small, divergence). Every cell above transcribed directly from the re-fetched March 2026 PDF, not scaled from the annual table -- closes this file's own previously-disclosed 'not cell-by-cell verified' gap outright rather than accepting the risk.

withholdingStructure.noCertificateDefault: WV/IT-104's own instructions don't state an explicit no-form default the way Kansas's KW-100 or Delaware's regulation text do; by this project's standing convention, absent a certificate the safer assumption is 0 exemptions and the higher-withholding two-earner table (not independently confirmed against a WV-specific statement this pass -- flagged as inferred, not sourced).

reciprocity.mechanism: Form WV/IT-104NR (the reverse side of IT-104), filed by the employee with the employer.
reciprocity.rule: A resident of Kentucky, Maryland, Ohio, Pennsylvania, or Virginia whose ONLY West Virginia-source income is wages/salary is fully exempt from WV withholding -- confirmed by direct quote from IT-104NR's own text: 'you are exempt from West Virginia Personal Income Tax Withholding.' Also covers military spouses under the Military Spouses Residency Relief Act via the same form.
reciprocity.confidence: primary_source_confirmed -- read directly off the actual certificate form, the strongest sourcing tier this project uses for a reciprocity claim (same tier as Ohio's IT 4NR, Kansas's KW-100 worked example). This is the LARGEST reciprocity cluster of any state in this project so far (5 states, vs. Wisconsin's/Michigan's/Ohio's 4-6 but WV's is unusual for a Mid-Atlantic-adjacent state) -- notably RECIPROCAL WITH VIRGINIA, which should be cross-checked against Virginia's OWN reciprocity list when VA is built (a natural consistency check, same pattern as this project's WI/MI/IL/IN five-state cross-check).

outOfStateConstructionRate.note: 1% surtax on top of the 8.5% base for out-of-state construction employers, per secondary sourcing.

unemploymentInsurance.confidence: cross_source_confirmed only -- workforcewv.org's own page gates the actual rate table behind an authenticated employer system, not a public static page; a direct fetch attempt confirmed this rather than assuming it. Wage base and new-employer rate are consistent across every secondary source checked with zero dissent.

localIncomeTax.rule: NOT a percentage-of-wages tax the way every other local tax in this project is (PA Act 32 EIT, OH municipal tax, MI city tax, Newark's payroll tax) -- West Virginia's local levy is a flat FEE PER PAY PERIOD, structurally closer to a fixed toll than an income tax. Several cities (Charleston $2.50/wk, Huntington $5/wk, Morgantown $3/wk, Parkersburg $2.50/wk) impose a mandatory 'City Service Fee' under WV Code 8-13-13, withheld by the employer from any employee whose DUTY STATION is in that city (i.e. work-location-based like Newark's, not residence-based).
localIncomeTax.confidence: cross_source_confirmed across multiple secondary payroll-industry sources with consistent figures; Charleston's own official fee-overview document exists but was only linked, not independently read as inline text this pass. NOT an exhaustive list of every WV municipality with a service fee -- only the 4 most commonly cited were captured, the same disclosed-partial-coverage convention this project used for Ohio's initial 3-city local pass before the full 679-municipality bulk load.
localIncomeTax.knownGap: This is a CLOSED-LIST-STYLE local tax structurally distinct enough (flat fee, not wage-percentage) that it would need its own new calc-code shape entirely if ever wired in -- not a reuse of Newark's employer-paid percentage mechanism or any existing local-tax dispatch.

paidLeave.rule: NONE for the private sector. West Virginia has no state-funded mandatory or voluntary Paid Family/Medical Leave program for private employers. SB 114 (2026 Regular Session) created only a narrow 2-year Paid Parental Leave PILOT PROGRAM for STATE EMPLOYEES (up to 12 weeks, birth/adoption/foster placement of a child under 12) -- out of scope for a general private-sector payroll engine, the same convention this project uses for public-employee-only programs.

exemptPretaxComment: RESOLVED this pass (was previously an open item with no array value at all, which broke the engine outright the moment WV got wired to calc-code -- ctx.taxableWagesFor() requires an array). Confirmed via W. Va. Code R. sec. 110-21-12 and secondary corroboration: West Virginia adjusted gross income of a resident individual starts from 'federal adjusted gross income... with certain modifications' -- same FAGI-conformity structure as Virginia. 401(k)/125/HSA/etc. deferrals are already excluded from FAGI at the point of measurement, and no modification found adds them back. Same confidence tier as Virginia's (this pass) and Indiana's/Kentucky's list-read confirmation.
knownGaps: WIRED to calc-code this pass (westVirginiaWithholding() in src/taxes/state.ts, method west_virginia_dual_table). Dispatches directly off input.payFrequency using the genuine per-period tables (no annualize/divide step) -- proven via 2 hand-derived tests in tests/engine.test.ts, describe('West Virginia'), one per earner-table.
Per-period bracket tables are now FULLY transcribed and wired (all 6 periods x 2 tables) -- this specific gap is closed, not just re-disclosed.

The 5% mid-year rate cut's own narrative (retroactive effective date, bill number) is cross-source only, not confirmed against tax.wv.gov's own 'Personal Income Tax Reduction Bill' page or bill text directly -- though the RATE TABLE itself (IT-100.2A) is primary-sourced and dated March 2026.

City Service Fee coverage is a 4-city sample (Charleston/Huntington/Morgantown/Parkersburg), not an exhaustive statewide enumeration of every WV municipality with WV Code 8-13-13 authority -- Ohio-style bulk-load-from-a-state-aggregator was not attempted because no equivalent statewide aggregator was found for WV's fee (each city sets and administers its own).
UI rate/wage-base figures are cross-source only -- workforcewv.org gates the actual current rate table behind an authenticated system, confirmed by direct fetch attempt rather than assumed.
exemptPretax RESOLVED (see exemptPretaxComment above) -- WV conforms to federal AGI, confirmed via W. Va. Code R. sec. 110-21-12.
No-certificate default (0 exemptions, two-earner table) is this project's standing convention applied by analogy, not confirmed against an explicit WV instruction the way Delaware's or Kansas's was.
